title: Soils
blurb: Which soil covers which state: alluvial, black, red, laterite, mountain, desert and more.
source: ICAR soil classification (alluvial, black, red and yellow, laterite, mountain, arid, saline and alkaline, peaty and marshy), summarised by state from NBSS&LUP and NCERT-style texts
licence: Public facts (ICAR classification), summarised by state; approximate
note: Shaded by the main soil of each state. Soils do not follow state borders, and saline-alkaline and peaty-marshy soils are patches, listed under the legend.

types.name: Alluvial
types.also: Gangetic and Brahmaputra plains, east and west coastal deltas. Most fertile, wheat and rice.

types.name: Black (regur)
types.also: Deccan lava plateau, also parts of Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu. Cotton soil.

types.name: Red and yellow
types.also: Eastern and southern Deccan on crystalline rock. Low in nitrogen and humus.

types.name: Laterite
types.also: Heavy rain with alternating wet and dry spells: Western Ghats, Kerala, coastal Karnataka, Meghalaya, Odisha hills. Cashew, tea, coffee.

types.name: Mountain and forest
types.also: Himalayan slopes and valleys, north-east hills. Texture varies with height.

types.name: Arid and desert
types.also: Thar desert (sandy, often saline), Ladakh cold desert.

types.name: Island and coastal sands
types.also: Island and small coastal territories: sandy and coral-derived soils.

types.name: Saline and alkaline (patches only)
types.also: Rann of Kachchh, Sambhar area, canal-irrigated parts of Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh.

types.name: Peaty and marshy (patches only)
types.also: Kuttanad in Kerala, Sundarbans, coastal Odisha, Bihar and Uttarakhand pockets.
